text.title: Product Launch Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding Product Launch. Each pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale; HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override. Rules r9–r19 fold in the former planning and execution files: the T-8-to-T+2 launch planning timeline, required assets, channel matrix rules, and positioning principles. Launch-day sequencing rules, monitoring requirements, post-launch actions, and the antipatterns that waste launch momentum. The antipatterns now live in `content/03-failure-modes.xml`.

rule.statement: Launch progresses through pre-launch / launch-day / post-launch gates; each gate has an explicit go/no-go check.
rule.rationale: Launch progresses through pre-launch / launch-day / post-launch gates; each gate has an explicit go/no-go check.

rule.statement: Audience is segmented (warm list, cold list, channel partners); messaging and timing differ per segment.
rule.rationale: Audience is segmented (warm list, cold list, channel partners); messaging and timing differ per segment.

rule.statement: Rollback plan exists and is rehearsed before launch day; no plan = no launch.
rule.rationale: Rollback plan exists and is rehearsed before launch day; no plan = no launch.

rule.statement: Launch monitors (errors, signups, revenue, support volume) armed before announcement; no monitor = no launch.
rule.rationale: Launch monitors (errors, signups, revenue, support volume) armed before announcement; no monitor = no launch.

rule.statement: Post-launch review at +14 days emits scale / hold / rollback; no review window = no launch.
rule.rationale: Post-launch review at +14 days emits scale / hold / rollback; no review window = no launch.

rule.statement: The launch MUST name exactly one primary positioning segment and one message for it. This is distinct from r2-segmented-cadence: the audience list is segmented for delivery (warm / cold / partners), while positioning stays singular. A launch whose landing page addresses three segments is rejected.
rule.rationale: Positioning aimed at three segments reads as aimed at none; the secondary segments are better served as derivative angles after the primary one lands.

rule.statement: Launch day MUST have a written runbook giving, per channel, a timestamp, a named owner and the reversal step for that channel specifically. A single global rollback_plan does not satisfy this.
rule.rationale: r3-rollback-precondition reverses the product; the per-channel steps reverse the announcement, and those are different actions with different owners — an unrecalled email blast survives a clean product rollback.

rule.statement: The channel plan MUST carry at least three activated channels across owned, earned and paid; a launch resting on one channel is rejected.
rule.rationale: Single-channel launches inherit that channel's variance in full — and the one channel teams most often lean on, press pickup, is the least controllable of the three.

rule.statement: Choose launch type before planning: soft launch (limited audience, low effort), beta launch (early adopters, medium effort), full launch (public, high effort), major release (existing users, medium effort). Each type drives a different asset set and timeline scope.
rule.rationale: A full-launch playbook applied to a beta wastes preparation time. Matching type to scope prevents over-engineering small launches and under-preparing large ones.

rule.statement: Lock the launch date 2 weeks out and treat it as immovable. Sliding a launch once erodes team trust and breaks partner commitments.
rule.rationale: Date slippage cascades to partner schedules, press embargoes, and pre-built social content. A locked date forces scope cuts instead of deadline cuts.

rule.statement: Minimum viable launch requires: landing page, demo or screenshots, announcement email, social posts (per channel), basic documentation. No launch without all five. Assign an owner and due date to each asset at T-8.
rule.rationale: The most common launch failure mode is assets discovered incomplete at T-0. Owner and due date at T-8 gives 7 weeks of remediation runway. The T-minus timeline itself is step 0 of `content/04-procedure.xml`.

rule.statement: Tailor message to each channel — same copy across all channels underperforms. Schedule announcements in sequence: email list first (warm audience), then social, then directories/press.
rule.rationale: Warm audiences convert first and create social proof for cold audiences. Reversing the sequence wastes the warm-audience advantage.

rule.statement: Launch on Tuesday or Wednesday, mid-month. Avoid major industry events (Google I/O, AWS re:Invent, WWDC weeks) and US public holidays.
rule.rationale: Thursday-Friday launches compete with end-of-week context-switching. Monday launches compete with inbox clearing. Mid-month avoids budget cycles and conference distractions.

rule.statement: Write a rollback narrative (200-word post explaining why the launch was paused) before T-Day. If you never publish it, no harm done. Without it, the decision to pause is made under stress with no preparation.
rule.rationale: Launch-day decisions made under stress produce poorly-framed communications. Pre-written rollback narrative is cheap insurance. Complements r3-rollback-precondition: that rule rehearses the product reversal, this one pre-writes the public explanation.

rule.statement: Assign a single launch DRI who can say no to feature creep in the last 72 hours. All other team members are in support mode. Kill switch is held by a human, not an automated agent.
rule.rationale: Launch-day decisions require context the automation does not have. An agent that auto-rolls-back on Twitter snark or a minor error rate spike will rollback unnecessarily and create a worse PR situation.

rule.statement: Verify core flows manually before flipping feature flags or sending any announcement. A broken user flow discovered after the email blast goes out cannot be recalled.
rule.rationale: Launch-day bugs that appear before any announcement can be fixed quietly. Bugs discovered after the email blast require a public apology email. Step 3 (dry-run) of `content/04-procedure.xml` is where this check runs.

rule.statement: Monitor: server health, error rates, signup flow conversion, and support queue length throughout launch day. Set alert thresholds before launch — define the number that triggers human escalation.
rule.rationale: Monitoring without pre-set thresholds means every small anomaly triggers a team-wide discussion. Pre-set thresholds route noise to silence and signal to humans. Extends r4-monitors-pre-armed: armed monitors are the floor, numeric escalation thresholds are the requirement here.

rule.statement: Capture testimonials within 48 hours of launch — that is when user goodwill peaks and permission to quote is highest.
rule.rationale: Testimonial requests sent 2 weeks after launch produce lower response rates and more generic feedback. The window closes fast.

rule.statement: Run a 30-minute retrospective within 7 days of launch. Force the retrospective agent (if used) to interview at least 3 customers before drafting — metrics-only retrospectives produce self-congratulatory artifacts that hide real learnings.
rule.rationale: Post-launch learnings evaporate rapidly as the team moves on. A 7-day hard deadline preserves institutional memory while it is still fresh. Distinct from the +14d scale / hold / rollback review in r5-post-launch-window: the retro captures learnings, the review makes the decision.

rule.statement: If preconditions in AGENTS.md "Applies If" do not all hold, OR any "Skip If" disqualifier is true, do not run this methodology — route to the named alternative.
rule.rationale: Methodologies are pre-condition gated; running them out-of-scope produces noise and burns the agent context budget.

rule.statement: If preconditions hold, execute the procedure in `content/04-procedure.xml` (or the rule set above when complexity is light), emit the artefact specified by `content/02-output-contract.xml`, and validate with `scripts/validate-product-launch.py` before returning.
rule.rationale: Tying the entry rule to the validator script closes the loop between policy and machine check.
